name: Bench Press
summary: The classic barbell press performed lying on a flat bench. It builds the chest, with the triceps and front shoulders assisting the press.
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with your feet planted on the floor and your eyes under the bar.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width and unrack it over your chest.
Lower the bar under control until it touches your mid-chest.
Press the bar back up until your arms are fully extended.

name: Incline Bench Press
summary: A barbell press on a bench set to a 30–45° incline. The angle shifts the work toward the upper chest and front shoulders.
instructions: Set the bench to a 30–45° incline and lie back with your feet on the floor.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width and unrack it over your upper chest.
Lower the bar under control to your upper chest.
Press the bar back up until your arms are fully extended.

name: Dumbbell Fly
summary: An isolation movement lying on a bench, opening and closing the arms in a wide arc with dumbbells. It stretches and squeezes the chest without heavy pressing.
instructions: Lie on a flat bench holding a dumbbell in each hand above your chest, palms facing each other.
With a slight bend in your elbows, open your arms in a wide arc until you feel a stretch in your chest.
Bring the dumbbells back together above your chest along the same arc.
Keep the elbow angle constant throughout; only the shoulders move.

name: Push-Up
summary: The fundamental bodyweight press from a plank position. It trains the chest, triceps, and shoulders while the core holds the body rigid.
instructions: Start in a plank with your hands slightly wider than shoulder width and your body in a straight line.
Lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows, keeping them at about 45° from your torso.
Stop just above the floor, then press back up to the starting position.
Keep your hips level and your core braced the whole time.

name: Cable Crossover
summary: A cable isolation exercise pulling both handles from high pulleys down and across the body. Constant cable tension targets the chest through its full range.
instructions: Set both pulleys high, grab a handle in each hand, and step forward into a staggered stance.
With a slight bend in your elbows, pull the handles down and together in front of your hips.
Squeeze your chest at the point where your hands meet.
Return your arms slowly to the stretched starting position.

name: Pull-Up
summary: A bodyweight pull hanging from an overhead bar with an overhand grip. It is the benchmark builder for the lats and upper back, with strong biceps involvement.
instructions: Hang from a bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder width.
Pull your chest toward the bar by driving your elbows down and back.
Rise until your chin clears the bar.
Lower yourself under control to a full hang.

name: Lat Pulldown
summary: A machine pull that brings a wide bar down to the upper chest while seated. It trains the same pattern as a pull-up with adjustable load.
instructions: Sit at the machine with your thighs secured under the pads and grip the bar wider than shoulder width.
Pull the bar down to your upper chest, driving your elbows down and back.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the bottom.
Let the bar rise slowly until your arms are fully extended.

name: Barbell Row
summary: A bent-over pull rowing a barbell to the torso. It builds thickness across the whole back and reinforces hip-hinge strength.
instructions: Hinge at the hips with a flat back until your torso is close to parallel with the floor, holding the bar with an overhand grip.
Row the bar to your lower ribs, driving your elbows behind you.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
Lower the bar under control until your arms are extended.

name: Seated Cable Row
summary: A seated horizontal pull on a cable machine. The supported position lets you focus on squeezing the mid-back through a long range of motion.
instructions: Sit with your feet on the platform, knees slightly bent, and grab the handle with both hands.
Pull the handle to your stomach while keeping your torso upright.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together, then let the handle return slowly until your arms are extended.

name: Deadlift
summary: Lifting a loaded barbell from the floor to a standing position. The heaviest full-body pull, driven by the back, hamstrings, and glutes.
instructions: Stand with the bar over mid-foot and grip it just outside your legs.
Set a flat back with your hips down and chest up.
Drive through your legs and stand up, keeping the bar close to your body.
Lock out your hips at the top, then lower the bar back to the floor with control.

name: Shrug
summary: Raising the shoulders straight up while holding a barbell or dumbbells. A simple isolation movement for the upper traps.
instructions: Stand tall holding the weight with your arms hanging at your sides.
Raise your shoulders straight up toward your ears as high as you can.
Hold the squeeze briefly at the top.
Lower your shoulders slowly back down; keep your arms straight throughout.

name: Overhead Press
summary: Pressing a barbell from the shoulders to overhead while standing. The core strength lift for the shoulders, with the triceps finishing the press.
instructions: Stand with the bar resting on your front shoulders, hands just outside shoulder width.
Brace your core and press the bar straight up past your face.
Lock out your arms overhead with the bar over your mid-foot.
Lower the bar under control back to your shoulders.

name: Lateral Raise
summary: Raising light dumbbells out to the sides until the arms are parallel with the floor. The key isolation move for wider shoulders.
instructions: Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with a slight bend in your elbows.
Raise your arms out to the sides until they are about parallel with the floor.
Pause briefly at the top without shrugging your shoulders.
Lower the dumbbells slowly back to your sides.

name: Front Raise
summary: Lifting dumbbells straight out in front to shoulder height. It isolates the front head of the shoulder.
instructions: Stand holding dumbbells in front of your thighs, palms facing your body.
Raise one or both arms straight forward until they reach shoulder height.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows and avoid swinging your torso.
Lower the weight slowly back to the starting position.

name: Face Pull
summary: Pulling a rope attachment toward the face on a high cable. It strengthens the rear shoulders and upper back, key for posture and shoulder health.
instructions: Set a rope attachment at face height and grab both ends with an overhand grip.
Pull the rope toward your face, spreading the ends apart as your hands reach your ears.
Squeeze your rear shoulders and upper back at the end of the pull.
Return your arms slowly to the extended starting position.

name: Barbell Curl
summary: The standing barbell curl, flexing the elbows to lift the bar from the thighs to the shoulders. The classic mass builder for the biceps.
instructions: Stand holding the bar with an underhand grip at shoulder width, arms extended.
Curl the bar up toward your shoulders, keeping your elbows pinned at your sides.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement.
Lower the bar slowly until your arms are fully extended.

name: Dumbbell Curl
summary: Curling dumbbells one in each hand, with a palms-up grip. The independent arms allow a natural wrist path and even biceps development.
instructions: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand, arms at your sides and palms facing forward.
Curl the dumbbells toward your shoulders, keeping your elbows at your sides.
Squeeze at the top, then lower the weights slowly until your arms are extended.

name: Hammer Curl
summary: A dumbbell curl performed with a neutral, thumbs-up grip. It shifts emphasis to the brachialis and forearms for thicker-looking arms.
instructions: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your body.
Curl the dumbbells up while keeping the neutral grip, like swinging a hammer.
Keep your elbows pinned at your sides throughout.
Lower the weights slowly back to the starting position.

name: Triceps Pushdown
summary: Extending the elbows to push a cable attachment down from chest height to the thighs. A staple isolation movement for all three triceps heads.
instructions: Face a high pulley and grab the bar or rope with your elbows bent at your sides.
Push the attachment down until your arms are fully extended.
Squeeze your triceps at the bottom, keeping your elbows pinned in place.
Let the attachment rise slowly back to chest height.

name: Skull Crusher
summary: Lying on a bench and lowering a bar or dumbbells toward the forehead by bending only the elbows. A focused stretch-and-extend movement for the triceps.
instructions: Lie on a bench holding the weight above your chest with arms extended.
Bend your elbows to lower the weight toward your forehead, keeping your upper arms still.
Stop just above your forehead.
Extend your elbows to press the weight back to the start.

name: Dip
summary: Lowering and pressing the body between parallel bars. A heavy bodyweight push that loads the triceps, with the chest and shoulders assisting.
instructions: Support yourself on parallel bars with your arms locked and body upright.
Lower your body by bending your elbows until your upper arms are about parallel with the bars.
Keep your torso upright to emphasize the triceps.
Press back up until your arms are fully extended.

name: Squat
summary: The barbell back squat: bending hips and knees to lower into a deep seat, then standing back up. The foundational lift for the quads, glutes, and overall leg strength.
instructions: Rest the bar on your upper back and stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart.
Brace your core and sit down by bending your hips and knees together.
Descend until your thighs are at least parallel with the floor, keeping your heels down.
Drive back up through your whole foot to a full stand.

name: Front Squat
summary: A squat with the barbell racked on the front shoulders. The upright torso keeps tension on the quads and demands a strong core.
instructions: Rack the bar on your front shoulders with your elbows lifted high.
Squat down keeping your torso as upright as possible.
Descend until your thighs are at least parallel with the floor.
Drive back up while keeping your elbows high so the bar stays racked.

name: Leg Press
summary: Pressing a weighted sled away with the legs while seated in a machine. It loads the quads and glutes heavily without balancing a barbell.
instructions: Sit in the machine with your feet on the platform about shoulder-width apart.
Release the safeties and lower the platform until your knees approach your chest.
Press the platform away until your legs are extended without locking your knees.
Keep your lower back against the pad throughout.

name: Lunge
summary: Stepping forward into a split stance and lowering the back knee toward the floor. It trains each leg independently, hitting quads and glutes while challenging balance.
instructions: Stand tall, then take a long step forward with one leg.
Lower your back knee toward the floor until both knees are bent about 90°.
Keep your torso upright and your front heel planted.
Push through the front foot to return to standing, then alternate legs.

name: Leg Extension
summary: Extending the knees against a padded lever while seated in a machine. Pure isolation for the quadriceps.
instructions: Sit in the machine with the pad resting on your shins just above your ankles.
Extend your knees until your legs are straight.
Squeeze your quads briefly at the top.
Lower the weight slowly back to the starting position.

name: Leg Curl
summary: Curling the heels toward the glutes against a padded lever in a machine. Direct isolation for the hamstrings.
instructions: Position yourself in the machine with the pad against the back of your ankles.
Curl your heels toward your glutes as far as you can.
Hold the contraction briefly.
Return the weight slowly to the extended position.

name: Romanian Deadlift
summary: A hip hinge lowering the bar down the thighs with knees only slightly bent. It stretches and strengthens the hamstrings and glutes.
instructions: Stand holding the bar at your thighs with knees slightly bent.
Push your hips back and lower the bar along your legs, keeping your back flat.
Descend until you feel a deep stretch in your hamstrings.
Drive your hips forward to return to standing.

name: Hip Thrust
summary: Driving the hips upward with the upper back resting on a bench and a barbell across the hips. The most direct heavy loader for the glutes.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your upper back against a bench and the bar over your hips.
Plant your feet flat, about hip-width apart, close to your glutes.
Drive through your heels and lift your hips until your torso is parallel with the floor.
Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower your hips with control.

name: Calf Raise
summary: Rising onto the balls of the feet and lowering back down, standing or on a machine. The standard movement for building the calves.
instructions: Stand with the balls of your feet on an edge or platform, heels hanging off.
Rise as high as you can onto your toes.
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower your heels below the edge until you feel a stretch in your calves.

name: Plank
summary: Holding a rigid straight-body position on the forearms and toes. An isometric staple that builds core endurance and stability.
instructions: Rest on your forearms and toes with your elbows under your shoulders.
Form a straight line from head to heels.
Brace your abs and squeeze your glutes; don't let your hips sag or rise.
Hold the position while breathing steadily for the target time.

name: Crunch
summary: Curling the shoulders off the floor toward the pelvis while lying on the back. A short-range flexion that targets the abs directly.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Place your hands behind your head or across your chest.
Curl your shoulders off the floor by contracting your abs, without pulling on your neck.
Lower back down slowly to the starting position.

name: Russian Twist
summary: Rotating the torso side to side while seated with the feet raised, often holding a weight. It targets the obliques through controlled rotation.
instructions: Sit on the floor, lean back slightly, and lift your feet with knees bent.
Hold your hands or a weight in front of your chest.
Rotate your torso to one side until your hands approach the floor.
Rotate to the other side in a controlled rhythm; each side counts as one twist.

name: Back Extension
summary: Raising the torso from a bent position on a hyperextension bench. It strengthens the lower back, with glutes and hamstrings assisting.
instructions: Position yourself face down on the bench with your hips on the pad and ankles secured.
Lower your torso toward the floor by hinging at the hips.
Raise your torso until your body forms a straight line — don't hyperextend.
Lower back down with control and repeat.

name: Treadmill Run
summary: Steady running on a treadmill. A full-body cardio staple for endurance and conditioning, with adjustable speed and incline.
instructions: Start walking at an easy pace to warm up for a few minutes.
Increase the speed to a run you can sustain for the planned time.
Run upright with a relaxed stride, landing under your hips.
Slow to a walk for a few minutes before stopping.

name: Stationary Bike
summary: Pedaling a stationary bike at a chosen resistance. Low-impact cardio that mainly works the quads while sparing the joints.
instructions: Adjust the seat so your knee stays slightly bent at the bottom of the pedal stroke.
Start pedaling at an easy resistance to warm up.
Increase the resistance or cadence to your working pace.
Keep a steady rhythm for the planned time, then ease off gradually.

name: Rowing Machine
summary: Rowing on an ergometer: drive with the legs, then swing the torso and pull with the arms. Cardio that works nearly the whole body, especially the back and legs.
instructions: Strap in your feet and grab the handle with both hands, arms extended.
Drive by extending your legs first, then lean back slightly and pull the handle to your ribs.
Return in reverse order: extend your arms, lean forward, then bend your knees.
Keep the strokes smooth and continuous for the planned time.

name: Elliptical
summary: Striding on an elliptical trainer with moving handles. Smooth, low-impact cardio that involves both legs and arms.
instructions: Step onto the pedals and grab the moving handles.
Start striding at an easy pace to find your rhythm.
Increase the resistance to your working effort, pushing and pulling with your arms as you stride.
Maintain the pace for the planned time, then cool down slowly.

name: Jump Rope
summary: Continuous jumping over a turning rope. Simple, intense cardio that builds footwork, coordination, and calf endurance.
instructions: Hold a handle in each hand with the rope behind your heels.
Swing the rope overhead and jump just high enough for it to pass under your feet.
Land softly on the balls of your feet with relaxed knees.
Turn the rope with your wrists, not your arms, and keep a steady rhythm.

name: Stair Climber
summary: Climbing continuously on a rotating stair machine. Cardio with a strength bias toward the quads, glutes, and calves.
instructions: Step onto the machine and start at a slow climbing pace.
Stand tall and rest your hands lightly on the rails without leaning on them.
Step fully onto each stair, driving through your whole foot.
Hold your working pace for the planned time, then slow down to finish.
